scene_translation: When you turned the key, the heavy door slowly opened. Inside was a small room that smelled of old incense. A single sheet of paper rested on a shelf, and you opened the notebook to look — written in a different handwriting from the previous pages, it said: 'Next, go to the old coffee shop in Suidobashi. The owner should know who you are.' When you looked up, a scrap of blue fabric had fallen in the corner of the room — there could be little doubt that the woman in blue had been here recently.
grammar_note: 【はずです】 'should be; ought to be' — expresses reasonable expectation based on evidence. 「<ruby>店<rt>みせ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>主人<rt>しゅじん</rt></ruby>はあなたのことを<ruby>知<rt>し</rt></ruby>っているはずです」= 'The owner should know about you.' Notice the polite です/ます register of the written message — it feels formal and deliberate, as if written for a specific reader.

mystery_memo: The notebook now contains a second message directing the player to an old coffee shop in Suidobashi, whose owner 'knows' the player — deepening the central mystery of who knows the player's name and why. A scrap of blue fabric confirms the woman in blue was in this room recently, possibly very recently. The notebook and locker key are both significant: the key has served its immediate purpose but may have a second use yet to be discovered. The grandpa from scene 3 mentioned a coffee shop in passing — this may be the same one, worth revisiting that connection.
